rationale.conceptual: Uses standard periodic DFT with PBE functional and dispersion correction, geometry optimization, and charge analysis—all textbook computational chemistry. No new theory or custom algorithm; the main challenge is correctly selecting initial configurations for multiple gas molecules, but that is routine.
rationale.execution: Pipeline has 4 stages: composite relaxation, band gap, 8 single-gas adsorptions (each with multiple orientation trials, ~24 relaxations), and a co-adsorption relaxation. Requires orchestrating many independent DFT calculations, managing input files, and post-processing energies and charges. Not trivially single-step, but the stages are repetitive and can be scripted with standard DFT codes.

difficulty.reasoning: Standard DFT study of gas adsorption on a composite material. Method is well-established (PBE-D3, geometry relaxation, population analysis). No novel algorithms, but requires careful setup of multiple adsorption geometries and calculations. Execution entails a pipeline of several relaxations but is scriptable. Resource needs are modest (small supercell, CPU-only).

compute_estimate.reasoning: The system is a 36-atom supercell with moderate k-point grids (6x6x1 and 8x8x1). DFT relaxations for such small systems can run on CPU with a few GB RAM; total input data is generated on-the-fly, no external dataset. The reference solve.sh suggests CPU-only environment.
